external_entities.name: customer
external_entities.description: A customer who browses and places orders through the mobile app and receives a faxed confirmation.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app
external_entities.notes: The text refers to customers collectively.

external_entities.name: marketing
external_entities.description: The marketing staff who maintain the catalogue spreadsheet.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application through which customers browse and order, and which talks to the web API.
processes.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app;

processes.name: web API
processes.description: The API used by the mobile app, storing customer information and handing orders to SIMS.
processes.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database
processes.notes: Nobody here can tell me what the API does about authentication.

processes.name: SIMS
processes.description: The stock and inventory system that receives orders, writes delivery addresses, and sends dispatch notes to the fax gateway.
processes.source_excerpt: SIMS does two things with an order.
processes.notes: The text also calls SIMS the stock and inventory system.

processes.name: spreadsheet macros
processes.description: Macros in the catalogue spreadsheet that send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
processes.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

processes.name: fax gateway
processes.description: The gateway that dials the number stored against an order and faxes a dispatch confirmation to the customer.
processes.source_excerpt: the fax gateway, which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it.
processes.notes: Nobody checks whether the fax arrived at the right place.

data_stores.name: user database
data_stores.description: The database containing customer names, addresses, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the user database is encrypted.

data_stores.name: flat file
data_stores.description: A flat file kept alongside SIMS containing only delivery addresses.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it — only addresses go in that file, nothing else —
data_stores.notes: Nobody here can tell me whether the flat file is encrypted.

data_stores.name: catalogue spreadsheet
data_stores.description: The spreadsheet used by marketing to keep the product catalogue, including prices and product copy.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Marketing keep the catalogue in a spreadsheet.
data_stores.notes: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

data_flows.name: browse and order
data_flows.description: The customer browses and places orders through the web API via the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Customers browse and order through our mobile app;
data_flows.notes: The customer acts through the mobile app; the flow is represented to the component that answers on the customer's behalf.

data_flows.name: talks
data_flows.description: The mobile app talks to the web API over HTTP.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app talks to the web API over HTTP — not HTTPS

data_flows.name: keeps customers
data_flows.description: The web API keeps customer information in the user database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web API keeps customers in the user database: name, address, and the card they paid with.
data_flows.data_description: customer name, address, and payment card

data_flows.name: hands order over
data_flows.description: When an order is placed, the web API hands the order over to SIMS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When an order is placed the API hands the order over to SIMS

data_flows.name: writes delivery address
data_flows.description: SIMS writes the delivery address into the flat file.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It writes the delivery address into a flat file kept alongside it

data_flows.name: sends dispatch note
data_flows.description: SIMS sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: it sends a dispatch note to the fax gateway

data_flows.name: faxes confirmation
data_flows.description: The fax gateway faxes the customer a confirmation containing their name and address.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which faxes the customer a confirmation with their name and address on it.
data_flows.notes: The gateway dials the number stored against the order and nobody checks it arrived at the right place.
data_flows.data_description: confirmation with customer name and address

data_flows.name: changes prices and copy
data_flows.description: The spreadsheet macros send SQL statements to the web API to change prices and product copy.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The macros in it send SQL statements straight to the web API to change prices and product copy

trust_boundaries.name: office
trust_boundaries.description: The office location where the marketing laptop hosting the catalogue spreadsheet is located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The spreadsheet lives on a marketing laptop in the office.

assumptions.assumption: The web API is reachable from the internet because Sokify sells online and customers use the mobile app to browse and order.
assumptions.basis: The system is described as selling online, with customers using the mobile app to access the web API.

assumptions.assumption: The mobile app presents a non-web interface because the text identifies it as a mobile app rather than a website or web application.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly says customers use a mobile app and that there is no website.

assumptions.assumption: The user database is confidential because it contains customer names, addresses, and payment card information.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database contains customer name, address, and the card they paid with.

assumptions.assumption: The flat file is confidential because it contains customers' delivery addresses.
assumptions.basis: The source states that only delivery addresses are stored in the flat file.
